description: Observe same-instance log extent immediately after write_atomically returns a serializer error following a successfully staged entry. Preserve immediate database metadata and later unrelated-commit/reopen observations as diagnostics, without expanding the formal length oracle.

harness.description: Open a fresh real PersistentStorage in a disposable workspace directory. Append one valid entry, then invoke write_atomically with a promise change and two entries, the second of which deterministically returns a serde error. Compare live get_log_len before/after the returned result. Drop storage before reopen and cleanup to respect RocksDB ownership.
semantic_changes: No target or database replacement. Use real persistent backend and native serialization calls.
Test Entry implements Serialize with a deterministic normal error for value 99; valid values serialize as u64. This supplies a fault through the declared fallible interface.
An atomic counter reports whether the failing serializer actually ran.

legality.derivation: The selected core crate already enables the persistent_storage dependency through its original dev-dependencies; no feature flags or manifests are changed. PersistentStorage accepts generic Entry + Serialize + Deserialize types and propagates bincode errors. A deterministic serializer Err, rather than panic or injected storage mutation, exercises the actual fallible helper path. Initial append and read establish a healthy existing extent. Ordered StorageOps are public API inputs; no core protocol history is needed to invoke this independently grounded storage rollback responsibility.
legality.applicability: Single writer and same live storage object, no crash or concurrent access, healthy local RocksDB and error returned during later-entry serialization. The directory is newly created under the disposable workspace, opened via the configured path, and closed before cleanup.
unresolved: Active persistent_storage compilation is determined by the trusted selected-target build. Native dependency build failure would leave observations unknown.
Core panic behavior and cluster consequences are outside this local interface check.

grounding.derivation: The actual write_atomically Result supplies the antecedent. get_log_len before and immediately after the same call supplies the rollback comparison; transaction identity is a separate label. This getter reads cached next_log_key minus persisted compaction state, so the result establishes an observable API-state discrepancy, not immediate durable log mutation. Later commit/reopen output is diagnostic and is not a second formal property.
grounding.applicability: Compare only returned Err outcomes after independent valid-state admission. There is no requirement that every call fail or that failed calls later succeed.
unresolved: No whole-cluster safety attribution follows solely from this getter comparison.

observable_properties.description: A returned error from an atomic transaction must leave same-instance observable log extent unchanged.

uncertainties: This formal oracle checks immediate observable extent; persistence and future-commit diagnostics do not broaden the obligation result.
A compilation or database initialization failure is not a property violation.
